steps.domain_action: Begin in void — no position, no exposure, only potential.
Enter a long position on a Kalshi contract based on a predictive thesis.
Chain multiple trades or adjustments as new information arrives.
The market bifurcates — one path where the event occurs (T), one where it does not (F).
On the T-branch, the event resolves affirmatively; the contract pays out.
On the F-branch, the event fails to occur; the contract expires at zero.
During the event window, conflicting signals create a B-state — both outcomes are simultaneously plausible.
Exit or hedge the position as uncertainty resolves.
Settlement merges both branches — capital is returned based on actual outcome.
Market closes — all positions resolved, boundary reasserted.
The trading algorithm logs its performance and updates its model — self-reference closes the loop.
Each trade is permanently recorded on the exchange ledger — irreversible and auditable.
